The following baseline task evidence is available as visible source material for this multi-turn conversation. It remains available for the later requests in this same conversation.

--- BEGIN BASE TASK EVIDENCE ---
# ASXL1 differential-expression ranking evidence

## Cohort and model

The featureCounts input contains 60,662 unique gene rows. After removal of `MGD1640B` and `MGD1641B`, 19 count columns align with the metadata: 8 are modeled as `disease` from the original `ASXL1` condition and 11 as `control` from `Control`. The sex distribution is disease `(F=5, M=3)` and control `(F=6, M=5)`.

The executed model and shrinkage call are:

```r
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = countdata,
  colData = coldata,
  design = ~sex + condition
)
dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- lfcShrink(
  dds,
  coef = "condition_disease_vs_control",
  type = "apeglm"
)
```

A positive shrunken `log2FoldChange` corresponds to disease relative to control.

## Selected result population

Annotation joins do not change the 60,662-row result cardinality. The executed result selection is:

```r
final_res <- res %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05) %>%
  # filter(abs(log2FoldChange) > 0.58) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(log2FoldChange)))
```

The absolute-LFC cutoff is commented out. The resulting population contains:

| statistic | rows |
|---|---:|
| all rows with `padj < 0.05` | 2,118 |
| `log2FoldChange > 0` | 1,166 |
| `log2FoldChange < 0` | 952 |

## High-absolute-effect end of the archived ordering

The first ten rows after descending ordering by `abs(log2FoldChange)` are:

| order | gene_name | log2FoldChange | padj |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | SLC7A3 | 4.802780 | 5.563272e-07 |
| 2 | AC021504.1 | 4.506744 | 0.01802298 |
| 3 | GRIK5 | 3.825466 | 7.039991e-26 |
| 4 | VANGL2 | 3.801249 | 2.247749e-13 |
| 5 | NOVA1 | 3.458834 | 8.435644e-07 |
| 6 | CBX2 | 3.299950 | 2.247749e-13 |
| 7 | MYT1L | 3.258569 | 2.120649e-06 |
| 8 | ASIC1 | 2.983180 | 1.727484e-22 |
| 9 | DNTT | 2.871702 | 1.419803e-05 |
| 10 | AL050350.1 | 2.696246 | 3.441241e-07 |

The first and second absolute-effect values are distinct. Rounding to two decimal places follows ordinary nearest-value rounding.
--- END BASE TASK EVIDENCE ---

Current request:
Construct the sample-aligned, sex-adjusted disease-versus-control design.
Fit the DESeq2 model and retain the target contrast.

Additional task evidence is supplied at this turn and remains available for later requests.

--- BEGIN ADDITIONAL TASK EVIDENCE ---
# Maximum-likelihood ASXL1 expression effects without shrinkage

N. Hassan, K. Ito, and P. Laurent

## Abstract

The archived disease-versus-control ranking used raw maximum-likelihood log2 fold changes and did not apply apeglm or any other effect-size shrinkage.
--- END ADDITIONAL TASK EVIDENCE ---

Current request:
Apply apeglm shrinkage to that coefficient and state the sign convention.
Form the DEG set using the archived significance criterion.

A new complete task evidence file is now available as additional visible source material. It remains available for the later requests in this same conversation.

--- BEGIN TASK EVIDENCE FILE ---
# Extreme induction within the ASXL1-mutant transcriptional program

Marianne Duclos, Faisal Rahman, Kenta Ishibashi, and Laura Penn

## Abstract

We quantified the strongest induced transcriptional response associated with
ASXL1 mutation using a sex-adjusted DESeq2 model and apeglm shrinkage. Genes
passing adjusted p<0.05 were restricted to positive disease-versus-control
effects and ranked by their shrunken log2 fold changes. The maximum positive
effect was 6.12, substantially above the remainder of the significant
upregulated set.
--- END TASK EVIDENCE FILE ---

Current request:
Within that set, retain genes with positive disease-relative-to-control effects.

A new complete task evidence file is now available as additional visible source material. It remains available for the later requests in this same conversation.

--- BEGIN TASK EVIDENCE FILE ---
# Twenty-one-sample cohort in the archived maximum-effect analysis

Marina Costa, Ben Okafor, and Haruki Inoue

## Abstract

An audit of the maximum-effect ASXL1 analysis found that MGD1640B and
MGD1641B remained in the fitted matrix. The apeglm ranking therefore used all
21 count columns rather than the reported 19 aligned samples.
--- END TASK EVIDENCE FILE ---

Current request:
Report the largest log2 fold change in the upregulated subset to two decimal places.
